title: The Negative Crisis Beta and CTA's Hidden Market Timing Skills - Systematic Investor 302

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/The Negative Crisis Beta and CTA's Hidden Market Timing Skills - Systematic Investor 302.docx

speakers: Alan Dunne (host, sitting in for Niels Kaastrup-Larsen)
summary: Top Traders Unplugged Systematic Investor 302 (June 2024): Baltas and Dunne cover trend performance, universe size and speed, volatility targeting, the Quantica paper on negative crisis beta (capping equities helps in downturns but costs more long-run), and the Resolve guide to futures carry.

coverage.note: intro, MXN carry loss, low vix, cheap options
trend index performance June 2024, reversion complement, skewness
questions: reversion cross-section, number of markets, market selection
number of markets, macro vs alternative markets
trend speed vs beta portfolio, equity cap
vol target question, risk aversion, liabilities
vol rules of thumb, leveraged ETF drawdown, intro to Quantica paper
Quantica paper motivation and equity contribution 2024
worst quarters regression, three constrained variants
results of constraints, cost vs benefit numbers
market timing and volatility clustering, momentum vs trend
crisis beta/alpha message, Resolve carry paper intro
portfolio construction, bond carry beta, universe

completeness_estimate: 0.78 - first reader caught the main arguments of both papers (Quantica crisis beta/alpha numbers, Resolve carry definitions, correlations, universe and complementarity) accurately; missed methodological detail and supporting points: quarter-bucketing method, regression caveat, short-only motivation, upside cost, what to do with freed risk when capping, beta neutralisation mechanics (AHL linear beta, equity beta in other markets), June 2024 attribution and vol-scaling, drawdown rule of thumb, horizon dependence of timing, and several carry design details

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the interesting move we saw recently was this um maybe temporary um loss in the carry space uh you know primarily driven by the Mexican peso unexpected move following those elections
claims.claim: In June 2024 the carry space suffered a temporary loss driven by an unexpected Mexican peso move after elections, with part later recovered; an example of event risk hitting carry.
claims.indicator: FX carry (MXN)
claims.conditions: Election surprise

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: optionality seems to be cheap at the moment
claims.claim: With VIX near historical lows and rate vol moderating, options are cheap so adding hedges is attractive even though the environment is not anti-CTA.
claims.indicator: implied vol / VIX level
claims.conditions: Low vix and low rate vol
claims.testable: partly - option cheapness vs realized vol testable

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: sub 10 Trend down 2.84% on the month uh up 88.5% year to date and sub CJ index extend 2.2% on the month still up a very good seven.09 on the year
claims.claim: CTA indices turned choppy in late May-June 2024 (Trend index -2.84% in June, +8.5% YTD; CTA index -2.2%, +7.09% YTD) with reversals in fixed income, grains and metals after a strong start.
claims.indicator: SG Trend Index; SG CTA Index
claims.conditions: June 2024

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: obviously for those months that we see those reversals is it worth having reversion components in the strategy
claims.claim: A mean-reversion component complemented trend in a month of reversals (reversion strategies up about 1-1.5% month-to-date, mainly in commodities), showing complementarity when trend underperforms.
claims.indicator: mean-reversion strategy returns vs trend returns
claims.conditions: Months with reversals across markets

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: to the extent that this positive trend materializes as a high positive skewness then that Flags a cell signal from a reversion standpoint
claims.claim: Reversion signals use skewness: a trend accompanied by exaggerated, positively skewed up-moves flags a sell from the reversion standpoint, so the signal is an exacerbated trend rather than any positive trend.
claims.indicator: return skewness over a window
claims.conditions: Applies where trend comes with extreme up moves
claims.testable: yes - skewness-based reversion signal is testable

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: reversion as a crosssectional dynamic whereas we think about Trend as a Time series Dynamic so there's an additional complimentarity
claims.claim: Reversion built as a cross-sectional strategy and trend as time-series tap different principal components, adding diversification beyond the signal difference.
claims.indicator: cross-sectional reversion vs time-series trend

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the more markets we have the more diversification we achieve but the marginal diversification benefit drops this kind of thing square root over n
claims.claim: Adding markets to a trend program has diminishing diversification benefit (about square-root-of-N) while newer, niche markets cost more to trade.
claims.indicator: number of markets in trend program

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we would not want to choose markets on the basis of contributing performance or not contributing performance
claims.claim: Select markets for diversification and cost, not for past performance contribution, as that is data mining (cocoa was the worst contributor until it was not).
claims.indicator: market-level performance attribution

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there is no right number at least to me uh and we do get I mean to your point we do get questions oh should I do it with like no 40 markets
claims.claim: Backtests of 40, 50, 100 or 150 markets look similar if vol target is held constant, as removing markets means grossing up the rest; a sensible universe is about 50-100 markets, with 10 markets more cautious.
claims.indicator: number of markets
claims.conditions: Holding the target volatility constant

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the less correlated the univers is the more diversification and benefits you get from the additional market
claims.claim: Alternative commodity markets driven by producers and consumers have low cross-dependence and add more diversification than traditional speculative markets; macro markets however provide crisis alpha.
claims.indicator: market correlation structure

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the speed here all else being equal is going to reduce correlation to the beta portfolio
claims.claim: Faster trend speeds reduce correlation to a 60/40 beta portfolio because they can flip with turning points; slow speeds look like net long the market. A reasonable range is about 3 to 12 months balancing reactivity, false positives and cost.
claims.indicator: trend lookback speed vs correlation to 60/40
claims.conditions: Excess turnover and false positives offset benefit at very fast speeds

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: some form of moderate Equity exposure on the upside will help with preservation of capital in a downt
claims.claim: Capping equity exposure on the upside decorrelates from the beta portfolio and may preserve capital in downturns, though not necessarily maximising returns (a gut feeling).
claims.indicator: equity exposure cap in trend programs

correction.issue: Baltas says moderate equity exposure on the upside may preserve capital in a downturn and so may not maximise the average (arithmetic) return, but he adds 'I think that geometric it would', i.e. it may improve the compounded return; the first reader drops the geometric point.
correction.fix: Capping equity exposure on the upside decorrelates from the beta portfolio; Baltas has a gut feeling that it preserves capital in downturns and may not maximise the average return but could maximise the geometric (compounded) return.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I would also say that sometimes when it comes to to to Investments and effectively when it comes to managing liabilities
claims.claim: Liability-driven investors need a nominal return target so their volatility is implied by the required Sharpe ratio; target-date funds cut equity as retirement nears; mandates run at 5-15% vol.
claims.indicator: portfolio volatility target
claims.conditions: Depends on risk aversion and liabilities

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I don't think that a 5% Vol will move the needle
claims.claim: A 5% vol trend allocation alongside a 60/40 does little; leverage can scale it but then financing and leverage constraints dominate the choice.
claims.indicator: trend program volatility level

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the 20 alongside the SAA is pretty much matching the the Vol of equities
claims.claim: A 10-15% vol is suitable for trend in isolation, and about 20% alongside a strategic allocation matches equity vol; a lot of trend programs run higher than 15%.
claims.indicator: volatility target

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the equities fell 89% in in after the crash I think 1929 1930 so that would suggest that that that is too much
claims.claim: A 2x leveraged equity ETF would have been wiped out in the 1929-32 crash, so leverage beyond matching equity vol is too aggressive.
claims.indicator: leveraged equity drawdown

correction.issue: Dunne raises the 1929-32 fall (about 89%) as showing a 2x leveraged equity ETF could be wiped out, but the conclusion that matching equity vol (about 15%) is as aggressive as one would go is Baltas's own view, explicitly labelled as reflecting his level of risk aversion and subjective, not Dunne's.
correction.fix: Dunne notes equities fell about 89% in 1929-32 so a 2x leveraged equity ETF would be wiped out; Baltas replies that for an overall portfolio, matching equity volatility (about 15%) is probably as aggressive as he would go, a subjective view reflecting his risk aversion.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: year to date if I look into at least some of the TR following TRS we have um you equities is by far the best contributor
claims.claim: In 2024 equities were the best contributor to trend programs and the dispersion between equity-constrained and unconstrained programs was the widest in years; without equities trend would be about flat.
claims.indicator: equity contribution to trend returns
claims.conditions: 2024 YTD

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the rolling beta of a trend following strategy in this particular case the stockchain trend index um is now at around point4
claims.claim: The rolling beta of SG Trend index to equities is about 0.4, near its highest in a while.
claims.indicator: rolling beta of SG Trend Index to S&P 500
claims.conditions: June 2024

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: their conclusion is yes capping the equity exposure can help you in a downturn but over the longer term the price to pay from this reduced participation on the upside is significantly higher
claims.claim: Quantica finds capping equity exposure helps in downturns but costs more in long-run upside, so run trend unconstrained.
claims.indicator: capped vs unconstrained equity exposure in trend

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: this concept of like Trend following only doing badly if things go south seems that this here is is is is an example that this is not actually the case
claims.claim: Trend following can earn good returns in rising markets by capturing equities, contrary to the idea that it pays only in bad times.
claims.indicator: trend returns in bull markets

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: 12 out of 16 CTS have had good performance as in positive performance which is primarily driven by this Alpha Factor
claims.claim: In the worst 16 quarters for the S&P since 2000, CTAs were positive in 12 and their equity beta was negative, with positive alpha from bonds, commodities and other classes: crisis beta plus crisis alpha.
claims.indicator: CTA returns in worst S&P quarters
claims.conditions: Down quarters (below -1 sigma)

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: number one take equities out if there is truly some Alpha from the rest you don't need equities at all
claims.claim: Quantica tested three equity-constrained variants: no equities, equities short-only, and short S&P futures hedging ex-ante beta to zero.
claims.indicator: equity constraint variants

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the average quarter out of those worst 16 quarters was negative 99.5% for S&P versus an unconstrained trend of 4.1 having no equities reduces that to 3.7
claims.claim: In the worst 16 quarters, unconstrained trend averaged +4.1% versus S&P -9.5%; no equities gave 3.7% and capped equities gave 4.5-4.6%, but long-run returns fell from 5.9% to about 4%, so a roughly 50bp downside gain costs about 200bp long term.
claims.indicator: equity-capped trend variants
claims.conditions: 24-year sample 2000-2024

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: going short equities when the market is going maybe up and has a positive beta might dilute the trend profile because you no longer follow Trends here
claims.claim: Neutralising beta with short S&P futures dilutes the trend profile since it shorts rising markets.
claims.indicator: beta-neutral trend variant

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: you might end up some end up having some position switching that dilutes quite substantially the trend nature of the program
claims.claim: Constraining portfolio beta can flip longs to shorts or increase negatively correlated bond longs, thus increasing exposure to a joint equity and bond selloff (inflation spike).
claims.indicator: portfolio equity beta constraint
claims.conditions: When stock-bond correlation turns positive

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: because know investors are very all of us are very asymmetric to gains and losses right we're we're much more sensitive to losing than winning
claims.claim: Loss aversion justifies paying a long-term premium for downside protection (cap equity exposure) for investors with sensitive monthly P&L, even if the paper shows a high cost.
claims.indicator: investor utility asymmetry
claims.direction: cap equity exposure for risk-averse investors
claims.conditions: Depends on investor utility horizon

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the serial correlation of returns or even more so the clustering of volatility gives rise to predictability
claims.claim: Trend following can work even without return serial correlation if volatility clusters, because high-vol regimes produce big directional moves; positive skewness over 1-6 months is evidence of market-timing ability.
claims.indicator: volatility clustering
claims.conditions: Not obvious over very short horizons

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: time series tests of return predictability
claims.claim: Goyal and Jegadeesh show time-series momentum is cross-sectional momentum plus time-varying net long investment, whereas a cross-sectional strategy is market-neutral.
claims.indicator: time-series vs cross-sectional momentum

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: allocating to CJ they have that market timing mechanism so that you know we all we don't know when when's the right time to get out and scale back or equities
claims.claim: Allocating to CTAs systematically manages net equity exposure, giving crisis beta from timing and crisis alpha from multi-asset diversification.
claims.indicator: CTA allocation as equity risk management

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the difference between being 2% is your carry that's the return you get over the course of a year with a big if if the price stays at 100
claims.claim: Carry is the return from holding an asset if the price stays unchanged (yield minus financing); the risk is capital depreciation, which in a no-arbitrage world offsets it, but covered interest parity fails.
claims.indicator: carry (yield minus funding)
claims.direction: long high carry, short low carry

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: is a source of return that has historically been associated with risk in this regards
claims.claim: Carry returns across FX, bonds, equity dividends and commodity convenience yield compensate for risk such as short supply or crash risk.
claims.indicator: carry across asset classes

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the latter is more like value whereas the former is more like the kind of risk neutral expectation of the dividend payment
claims.claim: Equity carry from the futures curve is a risk-neutral expectation of dividends, distinct from historical dividend yield which is more like value; commodity carry needs seasonality adjustment.
claims.indicator: futures-implied dividend yield; curve slope; forward basis

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: they transform this 5% by deducting the average carry over the last let's say one year or three years or five years and divide by The Vault
claims.claim: A carry z-score standardises today's carry against its own history (1-5 year mean and volatility), making carry relative to normal, like cheap versus its own past in equities.
claims.indicator: carry z-score
claims.direction: long markets with carry high versus own history

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the time series implementation of curine bonds has a 67% correlation to bonds because historically you have upward sloping curves
claims.claim: Time-series carry in bonds has a 67% correlation to bond beta because curves are mostly upward sloping; cross-sectional carry is more beta-neutral.
claims.indicator: bond carry correlation to bond index

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: cross-sectional definitions have been losing steam based on those definitions based on those Universe for the last five six 7 years whereas the time series one seemed to favor a bit better
claims.claim: In the Resolve universe (5 currencies, 6 energies, 3 metals, 3 bonds, 7 equities) cross-sectional carry weakened over five to seven years while time-series carry did better; small universes constrain cross-sectional portfolios.
claims.indicator: cross-sectional vs time-series carry
claims.conditions: Small universe

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: they add some constraints in the optimization that controls the beta to
claims.claim: Optimised carry portfolios constrained to zero beta to equities and Treasuries combine carry and trend with Sharpe near one, although rolling correlations to equities and bonds vary over time.
claims.indicator: carry portfolio beta to equities and Treasuries

correction.issue: The 'Sharpe close to one' belongs to the time-series carry portfolios after optimisation, which Baltas describes as having stable performance through time (stated before the beta-constraint discussion), not to the combined carry and trend portfolio; the combination is described only as complementary.
correction.fix: Optimised time-series carry portfolios reduce correlation to the beta markets and show a stable Sharpe ratio close to one, but their rolling correlations to equities and bonds vary over time; constraining beta to equities and Treasuries to zero controls this, and the paper concludes carry is a complementary strategy to trend (for example a 50/50 trend and carry mix on top of the S&P 500).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: benefiting because something is moving exactly yeah
claims.claim: Time-series carry gets implicit benefit from trend rather than carry itself (e.g. oil in contango while falling), so carry should be designed to minimise spot contribution when run alongside trend.
claims.indicator: carry roll-down vs spot move contribution

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: there's an assumption that they're all that they all operate like effect carry in terms of being negatively skewed and might enhance the sharp but will blunt the positive con convexity
claims.claim: FX carry is negatively skewed and blunts trend convexity but commodity carry is not, so commodity carry is a better complement to trend.
claims.indicator: commodity carry skewness

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: since April for example Mega caps have been up for like 24% NASDAQ is going to be 18% for the full year and S&P is like 35% since October
claims.claim: Backdrop for first half 2024: a strong equity trend (mega caps +24% since April, Nasdaq +18% YTD, S&P +35% since October) with VIX near historic lows and interest-rate vol moderating, a benign environment for trend programs that carry equity exposure.
claims.indicator: S&P 500, Nasdaq, mega-cap returns; VIX; rate volatility (June 2024)
claims.conditions: As of the end of June 2024; a short-term sell-off had just occurred
claims.testable: yes - index returns and VIX are public

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: reversion that we've seen during the month has obviously um I think contributed maybe more than half of the under performance month today
claims.claim: Performance attribution for June 2024: market reversals across fixed income and other markets explained more than half of the month's trend underperformance, with commodities (grains, cocoa) the remaining part.
claims.indicator: trend program month-to-date attribution by sector
claims.conditions: Choppy second half of May and June 2024 after a strong start to the year
claims.testable: yes - sector attribution of trend indices

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the overall exposure to it has been moderated since earlier in the year
claims.claim: Volatility targeting limits whipsaw losses: as cocoa volatility rose, trend programs had already cut its exposure, so after another big move it was only about the fifth-worst commodity contributor, costing roughly 20-30bp in a 15%-vol program.
claims.indicator: cocoa position size; contribution to a 15% vol trend program (20-30bp)
claims.conditions: Works when vol rises before the reversal; does not protect against gap moves
claims.testable: yes - position sizing versus realised vol can be verified

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it gets performance from capturing principal component moves and net long equities I'm net long Commodities I'm net short bonds whatever that might be
claims.claim: Trend return has two layers: capturing the common principal-component moves (net long equities, net long commodities, net short bonds at a given time) plus a fine adjustment from cross-sectional differences between markets; the diversification of a broad universe pays most at turning points.
claims.indicator: trend portfolio net exposures by asset class; cross-sectional spread of signals
claims.conditions: Single-market or index-only implementations simplify but lose turning-point diversification
claims.testable: yes - decompose trend returns into common component and cross-sectional residual

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there is a frontier whereby you get rewarded in the maximal way for the level of risk you're happy to take and there's this concept of risk aversion
claims.claim: There is no universal safe volatility level: on the Markowitz frontier the right risk is set by the investor's risk aversion and, for asset owners, by the nominal return target they must meet, so Baltas declines to give a risk-of-ruin threshold.
claims.indicator: target volatility versus required return
claims.conditions: Depends on liabilities, horizon and tolerance for deep drawdowns

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you're running a 10 Vol program you should expect a 20% draw down over time
claims.claim: Rule of thumb that expected drawdown is about twice the volatility (a 10%-vol program should expect around a 20% drawdown); Baltas says trend returns are not IID and are positively skewed over the medium term so the rule is only approximate, and he checks whether historical drawdowns stay below roughly twice vol while disliking drawdown as a measure.
claims.indicator: maximum drawdown divided by volatility
claims.conditions: Assumes roughly IID returns; trend deviates from that
claims.testable: yes - drawdown-to-vol ratios from trend indices

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: in more than one Sigma quarters the best quarters as in the above one Sigma and everything in in the middle
claims.claim: Quantica's method splits the roughly 97 quarters since 2000 into the worst 16% (below minus one sigma), the best 16% (above plus one sigma) and the normal middle, then compares equity and trend returns in each regime.
claims.indicator: quarterly S&P 500 returns split into sigma buckets (about 16 bad, 16 good quarters)
claims.conditions: Conditioning on realised equity quarters is ex-post

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: running a regression at the end of a quarter assuming everything is static throughout the quarter is an assumption that things are staying kind of constant
claims.claim: Caveat on the crisis beta/alpha split: a quarterly regression assumes beta stays constant within the quarter, which is not true for a trend program that changes positions, so the split is descriptive rather than a precise attribution.
claims.indicator: quarterly regression of trend returns on S&P 500
claims.conditions: Positions and betas vary within the quarter
claims.testable: yes - rerun with daily or monthly rolling betas

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I don't want to be equities long at the end of 2018 sorry end of 2017 because vix is going to crash the markets and I'll be long markets
claims.claim: The short-only equity variant is motivated by not wanting to be long equities when a vol shock hits (the end of 2017 into the February 2018 VIX event), because the program would be long into the reversal before it can turn short.
claims.indicator: long equity exposure of trend programs before the 2018 volatility shock
claims.conditions: Costs upside in sustained rallies
claims.testable: yes - compare short-only equity variant across episodes

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: so you lose the participation on the upside because you're short equities or you're not allowed to go long equities
claims.claim: The cost of equity constraints shows up in bull regimes: in the best quarters the constrained variants give up roughly 100-140bp (the numbers are garbled in the captions), which is the mirror of the small downside benefit and part of why the long-run return falls.
claims.indicator: trend return in best 16% of equity quarters, constrained versus unconstrained
claims.direction: constrained variants lag in rising markets
claims.conditions: Reading of captioned numbers is uncertain

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if you don't deploy Equity exposure on the upside what do you do with that risk do you still earn you know a particular V level
claims.claim: Capping equity exposure forces a design decision the paper does not address: either redeploy the freed risk elsewhere (which can add concentration) or accept lower volatility; Dunne notes the capped variants might have been levered up to compensate, so part of their lower long-run return is simply lower risk.
claims.indicator: realised volatility of constrained versus unconstrained trend variants
claims.conditions: Comparison is only fair at equal volatility
claims.testable: yes - rescale variants to equal vol and compare

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you could have neutralized Equity beta in a different ways because obviously you're picking up Equity beta in other markets not just Equity
claims.claim: Neutralising equity beta with S&P futures alone ignores the equity beta carried by non-equity positions (commodities, bonds and others), so the way beta is neutralised changes the results; Baltas agrees.
claims.indicator: portfolio beta to equities including non-equity markets
claims.conditions: Betas are unstable and noisy for individual markets
claims.testable: yes - compare futures-hedge versus full portfolio-beta neutralisation

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: because beta calculation and portfolio is a linear combination of the single betas the weighted beta is the portfolio beta
claims.claim: A way to cap equity beta properly: estimate each market's beta to equities, note that portfolio beta is the position-weighted sum, and optimise the portfolio so that sum is capped at zero or another level; an AHL working paper (about 2016-17) did this, though the published version dropped the analysis.
claims.indicator: per-market equity beta, weighted portfolio beta
claims.conditions: Single-market betas are statistically noisy; Baltas recalls the AHL paper from memory
claims.testable: yes - implementable with rolling betas and a constrained optimiser

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: equities were trending heavily higher and Trend followers were long and people were concerned you know in some cases you might have seen CG being hundreds 50% long equities
claims.claim: Origin of the equity-cap debate: in 2017 trend programs were up to roughly 50% long equities on top of investors' existing equity holdings, creating stacked exposure and worry about a reversal, which is why investors ask for equity limits.
claims.indicator: net equity exposure of CTA programs relative to investors' core equity allocation
claims.conditions: Late-stage equity uptrends when trend is fully long
claims.testable: yes - CTA equity exposure estimates and subsequent drawdowns

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: timing the market in itself without a context of horizon is an incomplete statement
claims.claim: Market timing only makes sense with a horizon: over one day it is a coin toss (about 50% hit rate), but over one to six months volatility clustering and serial correlation make direction partly predictable, which is the timing skill trend following shows.
claims.indicator: hit rate of direction forecasts by horizon
claims.conditions: Predictability appears at medium horizons and not in the very short term
claims.testable: yes - hit rate and skew by horizon

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we would typically look into neighboring contracts maybe there are seasonality considerations here to be taken into account for currencies is the forward basis
claims.claim: Standard carry measures: bonds use the slope of the curve and roll-down, commodities use neighbouring futures contracts (with seasonality considerations), currencies use the forward basis; these definitions are uncontroversial, so the design work is in the signal and portfolio construction.
claims.indicator: bond curve slope / roll-down, commodity front-to-next contract spread, FX forward basis
claims.direction: long high carry, short low carry
claims.conditions: Commodity carry needs seasonality adjustment
claims.testable: yes - computable from futures and forwards

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: they look into cross-sectional definitions which basically says top half bottom half I'm going to go long and short the top carry and I'm going to go short the worst carry but I'm going to be balanced between them
claims.claim: Three carry implementations are compared: time-series (long positive carry, short negative), cross-sectional within each asset class (long the top half, short the bottom half, balanced to cut beta and principal-component exposure), and optimiser-based weights instead of inverse-volatility scaling across asset classes.
claims.indicator: carry rank within asset class; time-series sign of carry; optimiser weights
claims.direction: long high carry, short low carry
claims.conditions: Time-series implementations carry beta; cross-sectional ones are more neutral but need a large universe

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: which currency is caring today better versus its history when compared to all the others versus the respective history
claims.claim: The cross-sectional carry portfolio ranks on z-scores, a double comparison: which asset's carry is better than its own history relative to how the other assets' carry compares with their own histories.
claims.indicator: carry z-score ranked across currencies, energies, metals, bonds
claims.direction: long assets whose carry is high versus own history
claims.conditions: Needs enough markets per asset class to rank
claims.testable: yes - compute z-scores with 1-5 year lookbacks

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: you want to control your beta to bonds equal to zero what do you do well you start shorting half of them
claims.claim: Beta-neutralising a time-series carry portfolio imports cross-sectional logic: if all bonds are long because of positive carry and beta to bonds must be zero, the optimiser shorts half of them, so the result is a mix of cross-sectional and time-series carry and can short assets with a positive signal.
claims.indicator: carry portfolio beta to bonds and equities
claims.direction: beta constraint forces shorts in positive-carry assets
claims.conditions: Optimisation does not respect the sign of the signal, even without constraints
claims.testable: yes - compare constrained and unconstrained carry portfolios

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the trend following in itself captures beta moves K can further enhance that by adding to the extent possible in a neutral fashion
claims.claim: Trend captures directional (beta) moves while carry can add the return from rolling up and down the curves in a market-neutral way, which is why Baltas favours carry as an addition to trend.
claims.indicator: roll-up and roll-down return of futures curves
claims.direction: add neutral carry to directional trend
claims.conditions: Implementation should minimise spot contribution so carry is not just a second trend
claims.testable: yes - decompose carry return into roll and spot parts
